title: Data centre operator DayOne reveals revenue surge in US IPO filing
source_used: Reuters text on The Edge Malaysia ('BENGALURU (Oct 5)' dateline); The Business Times (own reporting from the prospectus) for extra detail. Reuters original not opened (HTTP 401).
key_facts: DayOne Data Centers filed for a US initial public offering on Monday 5 Oct 2026, testing investor appetite for data-centre listings amid challenging market conditions.
Net loss of US$77.2 million on revenue of US$512 million for the six months ended 30 June, versus a loss of US$12.6 million on revenue of US$151.5 million a year earlier.
The filing comes as surging bond yields and elevated interest rates cloud the outlook for the fall IPO market, prompting several major listings to be postponed.

DayOne, Singapore-based, builds and operates data centres for cloud-computing and AI customers under long-term contracts, across Asia-Pacific and Europe; it began as GDS International, set up by Shanghai-based GDS Holdings in 2022, and was renamed DayOne in January 2025.
Offering size not disclosed; Reuters reported in February that it aimed to raise as much as US$5 billion at a potential US$20 billion valuation.
Proceeds are for new data-centre projects, working capital and general purposes; underwriters include Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, BofA Securities and Citigroup; planned Nasdaq symbol 'DODC'.

The Business Times (from the prospectus): one unnamed customer accounted for 69.2% of first-half revenue and 87% of revenue came from Malaysia; two existing customers are designated 'Chinese military companies' by the US Department of War.
quote_evidence: Data centre operator DayOne Data Centers filed for an initial public offering (IPO) in the United States on Monday, testing investor appetite for data-centre listings amid challenging market conditions.
The company posted a net loss of US$77.2 million on revenue of US$512 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a loss of US$12.6 million on revenue of US$151.5 million a year earlier.
The filing comes as surging bond yields and elevated interest rates cloud the outlook for the fall IPO market, prompting several major listings to be postponed.
why_it_matters_hint: A big AI data-centre company is going to the public market while rising yields have already delayed other listings.
